subject: Different Deviance Information Criteria Scores from R-INLA after update

messages.author: d815de9605bd63c3
messages.subject: Different Deviance Information Criteria Scores from R-INLA after update
parts:
Dear All
I am a Msc student and I wonder if I can be assisted with this scenario. I had run spatial temporal models in a previous version of R-INLA and had decided on the best model based on DIC. After I had updated both R and R-INLA to the most up to date version of each and run the models I get  different DICs from the previous. The  new DICs favour a different model than the previous one.
Any thoughts.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Different Deviance Information Criteria Scores from R-INLA after update
parts:
Minor differences in the DIC is to be expected, simply because of the
parallel computing. If the posterior is very flat, then the impact can
be larger. if you expect a flat posterior, you can try to do

r = inla(...)
r = inla.rerun(r)

which will restart at the current mode, which usually would stabalize
the results.

If there are any differences beyond this, please let me know.

Best
H

parts: Thanks Havard. The problem is to be resolved. However, I now have a technical question. I need to decide on the best model using DIC and WAIC. With my data using spatio temporal model on malaria count data, the scores favour a model of type II interaction seconded by the space time model proposed by Knorr-Held et al. (2000). Upon examination of the model with smaller DIC and WAIC seems  to behave strangely. I looked and the means of random effects they seem not to be uniform and they have a very wide confidence interval. I am inclined to opt for the second model  but I do not have a statistical reason for leaving out the model with the smaller DIC and WAIC. I have searched literature but cannot find any evidence to support my decision. Any assistance with this dilemma

I don't think DIC works well for space-time models at all. What kind of differences are you talking about?
E.g. is the difference in DIC ca 10 or ca 10000?

There is at least one paper discussing that DIC is bad for complex models (number of param ca equal to number of observations). I can try to find it if you want to?

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
